Executive summary

An asset-backed regional aviation platform

With a valuation of 46 million Euros, IAS Group presents an outstanding investment opportunity in the dynamic sectors of West Africa. Founded in the late 1970s to support Ivory Coast's agricultural boom, the group has since evolved into a versatile aviation enterprise, first of its kind in West Africa, serving key economic sectors including oil and gas, mining, and personal and medical emergency transport. Its growth trajectory has mirrored the economic expansion of the region, and it has demonstrated resilience and adaptability through various market and political conditions, managing to expand its services and geographic footprint significantly. With local companies across Ivory Coast, Ghana and Burkina Faso holding 5 Air Operator Certificates, and over 80 skilled employees, the group's local expertise and deep-rooted presence offer unparalleled operational continuity and responsiveness to complex situations.

Strategically positioned, the company taps into the most promising revenue streams, operating a proprietary fleet of 15 aircraft, with maintenance facilities in Ivory Coast and expansion potential in Ghana and Burkina Faso. The group's competitive edge lies in its rapid, informed local management decisions, robust offshore sector experience, and significant leverage from a strong client base in oil, gas and mining. It currently holds a monopoly offshore in CIV, a near-monopoly in onshore sectors within CIV and Ghana, and is unrivalled in Burkina Faso — ahead of competitors lacking critical local air operator certifications, experience and resources. The network synergy between the companies further differentiates them, enhancing technical support and business networking capabilities.

In the context of the aviation industry's strategic mergers, the company is poised to capitalise on emerging opportunities. Smaller, agile companies like this one are well-positioned to secure short-term contracts, particularly in the oil and gas sector, which can offer significant growth and development angles.

01 · Our founder and history

Our Founder and History

Four decades growing alongside West Africa

The group was initially founded in the late 1970s locally in Ivory Coast to accompany the country's agricultural expansion.

Over the years, the business has expanded alongside the commodities extraction and trading business, serving the agricultural, oil and gas (onshore and offshore) and mining sectors, then completing its services with personal transportation and medical evacuation.

The group is a pioneer in the region, being the first private aviation company in West Africa, and remains in a unique position today. Among others, IAS has been the first West African aviation group since 1981 in Côte d'Ivoire.

In the last decades the company has continued growing alongside the region's economic growth. In challenging years and periods of political crisis the business never stopped its expansion — on the contrary, social and political turmoil translated into high client demand for secure and emergency transportation of goods and people.

The group has expanded across sectors and geographies, with 5 local air operator certificates (AOC) and companies in 3 countries, adapting to local and international legal, compliance, regulatory and tax constraints. The corporate structure has been developed to optimise and adapt to these constraints.

03 · Market opportunities

Market Opportunities

IAS's revenue sources are among the region's most promising sectors

Oil & Gas

The oil and gas discoveries of Baleine and Calao by the Italian major ENI since 2021 have helped unlock the potential of the Ivorian offshore market, largely still untouched. Reserves are estimated at 2 billion barrels, and IAS won a 5-year tender in 2023 to continue supporting ENI. Several US companies including MURPHY and VALCO have acquired blocks and are preparing exploration campaigns; IAS recently participated in a tender for MURPHY's first drilling campaign at end-2025. Prospection results continue to be positive in Ghana, where VRAL is preparing to bid on upcoming tenders including for ENI. Further discoveries may be made in the Gulf of Guinea, where IAS can bid for contracts: Liberia, Guinea, Sierra Leone, Senegal, etc.

Gold

High gold prices continue to encourage exploration and production in Ghana, Burkina Faso and Côte d'Ivoire. In Burkina, this trend combines with declining security conditions, fuelling increasing demand for safe air transportation by both rotary and fixed wing. FAS is well positioned as a local company to respond to the growing demand. Similar business units could be developed in Guinea alongside the current business model and with guidance of current management.

Security

Given the versatile socio-political landscape of West African states, private air transportation will remain a privileged and key sector in times of crisis, for both private and institutional clients. Emergency evacuations, including medical, represent a growing business niche.

05 · Competitive landscape

Competitive Landscape

Offshore leadership and onshore monopoly

Offshore

On the offshore market in CIV, IAS has won all the O&G contracts. To our knowledge, the only competitor used to be NHV, which is to depart the country at end-2025. In Ghana, VRAL has a single competitor, Heliconia. Other helicopter providers contest these markets during O&G tenders, but have no permanent presence in CIV or Ghana.

Main competitive advantages

  • Local management enabling rapid, informed decisions in crises (epidemics, political change, terrorist attacks) and permanent client engagement
  • Local staff, including country-based pilots and engineers, ensuring operational continuity
  • Local knowledge of decision makers, processes and ways of doing business
  • Longstanding offshore experience — the first helicopter company operating in West Africa
  • Control of the value chain and operational autonomy as maintenance centre for its aircraft
  • Client-base leverage: synergies between Ghana and CIV for O&G customers present in both
  • Local air operator certificates (IAS in CIV, VRAL in Ghana) — the main regulatory barrier to entry

Onshore monopoly

In the onshore sector in CIV and Ghana, IAS, MAXAIR and VRAL so far own a monopoly. In Burkina Faso, FAS shares the private aviation market with a local broker (Air Sarada) and Global Aviation, the aviation arm of an African security operator — both lacking aviation experience and know-how. FAS offers unrivalled services with adequate technical and human resources and the support of the Abidjan and Accra bases. The support network between the three companies is itself a differentiator, enabling technical backup and efficient business development.

Current context

Global rearmament diverts aircraft, spare parts and human resources from the private sector. IAS has invested heavily in recent years to grow its fleet, strengthen maintenance capacity and reinforce HR to gain autonomy. A merger trend among offshore helicopter providers is reducing the number of players; smaller companies such as IAS are well placed to capture shorter-term contracts — a strong entry point into O&G.

09 · Operating terms and principles

Operating Terms & Principles

Predictable maintenance economics and a safety-first culture

Contracting terms: SBH & PBH

  • Safran SBH contract (Safran Turbomeca Support-by-the-Hour) — 5-star Business complete engine maintenance standard-exchange contract
  • Full Airbus Helicopters PBH contract (Parts-by-the-Hour for the aircraft cell)
  • Scope: H145 and all Dauphin N3 + Squirrel B2 (engine only). All rotational spare parts, main components included — engines, blades, main gearbox

Principle. The manufacturer receives a full data record of each engine/aircraft entering the fleet, updated monthly. This lets it provide preferred spare-parts availability for both expected (calendar / potential reached) and unexpected cases at no extra cost; the operator is charged by the hour.

Financial predictability, operational continuity and the highest standards of maintenance — at no extra cost.

Principles

  • Gold Member of the BARS programme
  • Member of HeliOffshore
  • Local content priority in Ghana, Côte d'Ivoire and Burkina Faso
  • Continuous improvement of safety, security, health and environmental policies
  • Operational autonomy and competitiveness thanks to regional scope
  • Airbus Helicopters maintenance centre since 2014

Climate-change commitment

  • Fleet renewal has started with the first H145, enabling newer, less polluting aircraft and sustainable aviation fuels
  • IAS is proud to support ENI's Baleine project — the largest of its kind in the region and a pioneering "zero gas emissions" project

10 · Our clients

Our Clients

Majors, miners, institutions and governments

Oil & gas companies

Majors such as ENI CI, mid-size producers such as Canadian Natural Resources, and local producers such as Petroci CI 11 and Foxtrot.

ENI has trusted IAS since it started exploring offshore Ivory Coast in 2021. After the discovery of Baleine and the start of production, ENI awarded IAS the exclusive transportation of its passengers and VIPs.

CNR decided to break its contract with its former provider and come back to IAS due to the competitiveness of its offers.

Mining companies

Direct PAX-transport users include Perseus Mining, Endeavour Mining, Montage Gold, Barrick Gold, Roxgold and others.

All producing mining companies in Ivory Coast and Ghana, and most of those in Burkina Faso, use IAS for bullion/gold transportation. Contracts are managed by Brinks Global — a historical client of close to two decades and IAS's sole-provider relationship for precious-metals transport in all three countries.

Others

Large international and local private companies, financial institutions, local ministries and governments, and medical institutions needing private transportation on a mainly ad-hoc basis.

Ratio analysis

Current ratio measures the ability to pay short-term obligations; above 1 means current assets exceed current liabilities. Below 1 may simply reflect a lean working-capital structure. Debt ratio shows the share of assets financed by liabilities (the workbook's liabilities side includes equity, hence 1.0).

Net margin: profit left per euro of revenue. ROA: how efficiently assets generate income. Asset turnover: revenue generated per euro of assets. P/E and P/B use the DCF valuation against 2024 net result and total assets.

Scenario notes

1. High growth. Projects cash flows over the horizon on the recent high-growth trajectory across subsidiaries — strong market potential and an accelerating expansion phase.

2. Steady growth. Turnover grows at a steady rate reflecting the current strategic plan (market penetration, geographic expansion, new services). This is the model's central case.

3. Moderate growth. A conservative case reflecting a mature, stable environment with limited expansion.

14 · Appendix

Appendix

Methodology, historical performance and contacts

Blended valuation methodology

1. Discounted cash flow (DCF) — weight. Captures intrinsic value from projected free cash flows of IAS, MAXAIR and FAS, applying a discount rate to the case, giving .

2. EBITDA multiple — weight. A multiple of applied to 2025 projected EBITDA, giving . Aviation services, fleet management and contract-based support businesses with steady cash generation typically trade at 6.5x–8.5x EBITDA, so 5.0x is conservative.

3. Revenue multiple — weight. A multiple on 2025 projected turnover, giving . Companies with long-term service contracts and asset-backed revenue often trade at 1.5x–2.0x; the weight is kept low to avoid over-emphasising top-line figures.
